fast.output: Well, we've got a tunneling system designed to reduce traffic congestion and improve safety. We're building tunnels at a rate that's quite fast, but not so fast that we compromise the quality. So far, we've built several tunnels in Los Angeles, Las Vegas, Chicago, Boston, and Washington D.C. We've got a lot going on, and we're working hard to accelerate the construction process, but we don't want to sacrifice quality. So, it's a balance between speed and quality. thinking.output: Well, I think it's actually not that hard to solve traffic problems. I mean, if we just had a boring tunnel under every major city in the world, then traffic wouldn't exist. That's a pretty small number of tunnels. We could put a tunnel under every major city, which would solve all traffic. That's what I think would solve traffic. queries.query: Explain your vision for sustainable energy

fast.output: Well, I think it's really important to just transition to renewable energy sources because fossil fuels are finite. And so, obviously, wind and solar are better than coal and gas, but they are intermittent. So, we need something more durable than wind and solar. And what that is, is power storage. That's why I'm working on Starlink, which is a satellite constellation to provide global internet and also power distribution. And then, if there's a grid-scale battery, and a network of small cells and satellites, then we've got a scalable solution to store excess energy when the sun isn't shining and distribute it when the sun is shining. So, my view is, let's make sure we don't run out of batteries. That's what we should be focusing on. Solar and wind are great, but we need a lot more than that to solve this problem.

queries.query: What do you think about AI safety?

fast.output: I mean, we have to be careful with superintelligent machines. If they're smarter than us, we could lose control of them and that's a risk. So, I think it's like, really important to make sure that superintelligent machines don't become a threat to humanity. We want to make sure that they're aligned with human values. And that means making sure that their goals are not incompatible with ours. And if there is a possibility of creating a superintelligent machine that could become hostile, then we need to take steps to prevent that from happening. It's possible that this might happen and we'll find out in a few years. But I'm pretty optimistic about the future. I think we can make a superintelligent machine that's friendly towards humans. But we have to be very careful. This is a big deal.

thinking.output: Well, I mean, I'm actually quite optimistic about the future of AI, but we have to make sure that AI is aligned with human values. I think there's a lot of work to be done in terms of ensuring that the AI is not a threat to humanity. So, if they don't, then, you know, we'll all be extinct. So, that's a big risk, but I'm actually very hopeful because I think the progress that's being made in AI research is tremendous. queries.query: How do you balance running multiple companies while also working on Neuralink?

fast.output: Well, I think the key is that I have a very focused set of priorities and goals for each company. For example, Tesla has a very clear mission, which is to accelerate the world's transition to sustainable energy. And then SpaceX has a very clear mission, which is to enable humanity to become multiplanetary. And Neuralink has a mission of making the human brain-machine interface more effective. So, my focus is on those three things, and then I try to delegate tasks to the best people at Tesla, SpaceX, and Neuralink to make sure we're all aligned towards those goals. It's not about juggling multiple balls in the air. I'm trying to advance these fundamental technologies that can solve big problems. And then I also try to be visible and engaged with our customers and stakeholders to understand their needs and provide value. That's really what it comes down to.

thinking.output: Well, I think one of the things that people don't realize is how much work goes on behind the scenes at Neuralink.
